sources.method: width = 25.4*D*a/sqrt(a^2+b^2), height = 25.4*D*b/sqrt(a^2+b^2), rounded half-up to 0.1 mm. D = 4.0 in, a:b = 1272:1080 taken exactly from resolution_px (square pixels assumed); the published diagonal is assumed exact (OEMs round it). Inputs: diagonal_in from the sources[] entry for 'displays[1].diagonal_in' <https://www.motorola.com/us/en/p/pmipmjq44ms>; resolution_px from the sources[] entry for 'displays[1].resolution_px' <https://www.motorola.com/us/en/p/pmipmjq44ms>. notes: CONFIRMED TO EXIST. US name 'motorola razr+ - 2026' and global name 'motorola razr 70 plus' are ONE physical device, stated by Motorola: the April 29, 2026 press release pairs 'the new motorola razr+ – 2026' (United States) with 'motorola razr 70 plus ... in Europe, Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific'. Corroborated by identical geometry on motorola.com/us (pmipmjq44ms), motorola.com/gb (pmipmjq45m3) and Motorola Support US a_id 192376: 88.09 x 73.99 x 15.32 closed, 171.42 x 73.99 x 7.09 open, 189 g. Motorola's support page spells the global name 'razr 70+' while its GB product page spells it 'razr 70 plus' - both are in aliases. MAIN DISPLAY RESOLUTION LEFT NULL - MOTOROLA CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE SAME PAGE: the spec table on motorola.com/us states 'Main Display:165Hz Display Resolution: 1084 x 2640 FHD+' while that same page's display_type meta string states '6.9" FHD+ (2640 x 1080), pOLED, 3000 nits, 165Hz'. 1084 and 1080 cannot both be right and nothing published by Motorola settles it; motorola.com/gb and Motorola Support a_id 192376 publish no main-panel resolution at all, so the value is null rather than a guess. The cover resolution (1272 x 1080) is not in dispute and is recorded. Main-display aspect also left null: motorola.com/us prints '22:09' and motorola.com/gb prints the corrupt value '0.9229166666666667'. Note the closed/open dimensions and 189 g are identical to the 2025 Razr+; that is Motorola republishing the same chassis figures, and each generation's numbers were taken from its own page, never carried across. Panel recorded OLED from Motorola's 'LTPO Extreme AMOLED' (main) and 'LTPS Extreme AMOLED' (cover). free_stop true from the press release's Flex View statement, which covers all three 2026 razr devices ('their razrs'); unlike the razr and razr ultra pages, this model's own product pages do not mention Flex View. announced/released via a web.archive.org snapshot dated 2026-05-21 (motorolanews.com returns HTTP 403 directly); May 21 is the US on-sale date. crease null - never stated. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence).
